messages:
maria: heads-up 9eu-west canary showing a jump in TLS handshake failures starting ~09:05 UTC right after we merged the RBAC tighten. clients failing with short-lived handshake aborts, looks like SNI routing + cert availability issue.

incident-bot: alert: tls_handshake_failures spike service=keystore-proxy region=eu-west count=210 window=10m

dmitri: digging into keystore-rotator logs: we're seeing two patterns: 1) 403 from keystore-store when rotator tries GET /v1/certs, 2) KMS AccessDenied when code retries to unwrap locally. sample log:

```
WARN  rotator.fetch - keystore-store returned 403 for /v1/certs?request=abc123
ERROR rotator.kms - KMS AccessDenied: arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:...:key/... cannot be used to decrypt
```

kelsey: timeline check: RBAC policy PR 4671 removed the `keystore-reader` binding from group `platform-service-accounts` at 09:00 UTC. That group includes the instance profile used by rotator. Seems like the rotator lost permission to call keystore-store after the merge.

ben: consequence: when certs are missing, edge proxies try to resume sessions (session tickets enabled) which can forward mismatched SNI and cause handshakes to abort. We saw a cluster of `session-resume` failures in proxy logs.

sre-oncall: quick patch: re-grant `keystore-reader` in eu-west to platform-service-accounts and restart rotator pods in canary only. Also disabled session-ticket resume on canary edge proxies. Doing now.

incident-bot: action: iam.binding.apply by maria 9canary namespace updated at 09:18 UTC

maria: canary rotator restarted, keystore-store 200s resumed for rotator. TLS failures dropped ~2 minutes after restart. Will roll fix to remaining eu-west namespaces after validation.

dmitri: root cause summary draft: RBAC roll removed read binding -> rotator received 403 -> rotator falls back to an alternate code path that invokes KMS unwrap directly under a different service identity which lacked decrypt permission -> KMS AccessDenied observed -> resulting absence of valid certs caused proxies to fail mTLS and session-resume attempts exposed SNI-routing mismatches.

kelsey: a few follow-ups for immediate backlog:
- add pre-merge check in infra CI that verifies critical service accounts (rotator/keystore) keep keystore-reader in all regions (owner: maria)
- add monitoring rule: alert on >10 403s from keystore-store for same service account within 2m (owner: dmitri)
- split KMS AccessDenied into its own alert channel (owner: dmitri)
- make direct KMS unwrap an explicit opt-in dev flag `ENABLE_DIRECT_KMS_UNWRAP` (owner: runtime team)
- add canary proxy config to disable session-ticket resume during cert instability windows (owner: sre)

ben: compliance note: we need to produce an audit packet for Oct 2; include keystore-store request logs, rotator instance ids, IAM state snapshot pre-change, and KMS deny entries. Also need to show we applied fix and the rollout plan. I'll collate. (owner: ben)

maria: I'll add a rollback guard script that blocks merges which remove any members of a preserved-binding list. Also will add a post-merge job that validates runtime services still receive expected 200s for critical endpoints.

dmitri: implementation detail: rotator code currently silently tries direct unwrap on 403s; change to record a `fallback_attempt` metric and emit structured log with original request-id + principal so we can trace. No automatic fallback until opt-in flag enabled.

sre-oncall: note on proxy mitigation: toggling `session_ticket_enabled=false` on canary reduced noise and sped recovery. We should add this to our emergency proxy playbook.

kelsey: tagging Sev3, will escalate if similar symptoms appear in other regions. I'll draft incident summary and link PRs: infra guard, rotator flag, alerts, and proxy playbook. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
